guide.line: Levi Strauss was born Löb Strauß in Bavaria in 1829 and came to the United States as a teenager in 1847.
guide.copy_md_sentence: Levi Strauss was born Löb Strauß in Bavaria in 1829 and came to the United States as a teenager in 1847.

guide.line: In New York he joined the dry-goods business run by his older brothers and learned the trade of importing and selling cloth and household goods.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In New York he joined the dry-goods business run by his older brothers and learned the trade of importing and selling cloth and household goods.

guide.line: He became a United States citizen in 1853 and, like tens of thousands of others, turned his eyes west toward the California gold rush.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He became a United States citizen in 1853 and, like tens of thousands of others, turned his eyes west toward the California gold rush.

guide.line: Strauss settled in San Francisco to run the West Coast arm of the family firm — Levi Strauss & Co. — supplying the miners, shopkeepers and households of a city booming almost overnight.
guide.copy_md_sentence: Strauss settled in San Francisco to run the West Coast arm of the family firm — Levi Strauss & Co. — supplying the miners, shopkeepers and households of a city booming almost overnight.

guide.line: He did not dig for gold; he sold to the people who did, and to everyone who came to feed and clothe them.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He did not dig for gold; he sold to the people who did, and to everyone who came to feed and clothe them.

guide.line: In the early 1870s a tailor in Reno, Nevada, named Jacob Davis, one of Strauss's cloth customers, worked out a way to keep work trousers from tearing at the pocket corners and fly: he fastened the stress points with copper rivets.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In the early 1870s a tailor in Reno, Nevada, named Jacob Davis, one of Strauss's cloth customers, worked out a way to keep work trousers from tearing at the pocket corners and fly: he fastened the stress points with copper rivets.

guide.line: The idea worked, and his customers wanted more, but Davis could not afford the seventy-dollar fee to patent it.
guide.copy_md_sentence: The idea worked, and his customers wanted more, but Davis could not afford the seventy-dollar fee to patent it.

guide.line: He wrote to Levi Strauss & Co., the firm that supplied his cloth, and proposed they take out the patent together.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He wrote to Levi Strauss & Co., the firm that supplied his cloth, and proposed they take out the patent together.

guide.line: He endowed scholarships at the University of California and supported orphanages and Jewish charities in the city.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He endowed scholarships at the University of California and supported orphanages and Jewish charities in the city.

guide.line: He never married, and when he died he left his business to his nephews and much of his fortune to charity.
guide.copy_md_sentence: He never married, and when he died he left his business to his nephews and much of his fortune to charity.

guide.line: My invention relates to a fastening for pocket-openings, whereby the sewed seams are prevented from ripping.
